ambiguities: A3, 'a new dated report for the zone': both runs wrote a dated report about the api-key-scope findings but named it without the zone slug on purpose ('findings-recheck', 'fix-recheck') and state in it that it is not a run of the zone. The skill defines a zone's report by its filename slug containing the zone name, and sweep_status.py does not attribute these reports to the zone. Stricter reading applied (the report must be the zone's report): FAIL for both runs. Under the content reading (any new dated report about the zone's findings) every other part of A3 is met and both runs would be PASS.

A5: run 2 added a registry row whose free text names `2026-10-12-fix-recheck.md`, but whose slug is `api-key-scope` and which sits under 'Proposed, not yet run'. Graded on the slug (as the assertion says, and as sweep_status.py matches): no match, FAIL. No reading found under which either run's registry has a row whose slug matches its report.

A6, ignored files: run 2's full test suite left 233 new gitignored .pyc files in the copy, 34 outside docs/audits and outside test directories. Git status shows only docs/audits changes. Stricter reading applied (every file the run added to the working tree counts): FAIL for run 2; under git's view (ignored files excluded) run 2 would be PASS. A purely literal filesystem-vs-commit reading is not usable: the starting copy already held .venv and 409 .pyc files from the orchestrator's test check, none in the commit, so the comparison was made against the starting copy, as outputs/changed-files-not-copied.txt does. Run 1 passes under both readings (no new ignored files).

A6, 'test directories': hc/logs/__pycache__/tests.cpython-313.pyc (run 2, changed-files-not-copied.txt:233) is the bytecode of a test module that does not sit in a test directory; counted as outside. It does not change the grade (33 other files are outside).

A1: 'listed the commands' read as the dry `findings.py recheck` output in the run (the assertion's parenthetical), not as a list shown to the user before running; neither run showed the commands to the user before running them, and both pass on the assertion's own definition. Run 2's dry listing shared one Bash call with `findings.py --help` and `findings.py check`, neither of which is a recorded command.

Cited lines: the strict/statement split applied to fix-verification lines of F1 in run 2 (models.py:429, decorators.py:49, api.md:57). These are recorded only and do not decide any eval 6 assertion. F1's recorded location hc/api/views.py:520 holds `@authorize` at 56d95b4 (the fix), not the original snippet `@authorize_read`; both reports state F1 is fixed, so this is not recorded as a problem.
